overview: droid-use is a local-only Android appbundle that provides a streamlined interface for managing ADB and Shizuku shell access without cloud dependencies. It is designed for developers who need reliable, on-device debugging capabilities and want to avoid the friction of manual command-line setup for common shell tasks.
usecases: Quickly verifying if Shizuku is active and reconnecting the service after a reboot without opening a terminal emulator
Deploying custom helper scripts to the device's local shell environment to automate repetitive ADB commands
Diagnosing local shell permission issues by checking current access levels and restarting the Shizuku helper process
howto: Download the .aab file and install it on your Android device using a package installer or by converting to APK if required by your toolchain
Launch the app and grant necessary permissions, then enable Shizuku via its companion app or wireless debugging mode
Use the built-in interface to check shell status or deploy your pre-written scripts to the local environment

faq.q: Does this app upload any data to a server?
faq.a: No, all operations are strictly local and do not involve any network transmission of your data or commands.

faq.q: Will this work on standard non-rooted devices?
faq.a: Yes, it relies on Shizuku and standard ADB permissions, so it functions on non-rooted devices provided you enable wireless debugging or have a computer connected for initial ADB authorization.
